payment_autopay_failure.name: Autopay / mandate / payment failures
payment_autopay_failure.definition: Instalments are missed, fail or are debited wrongly because of autopay, mandate, bank or payment problems, or because there is no auto-debit and the investor must pay manually each month.
payment_autopay_failure.question: stop

missing_sip_controls.name: Can't pause, skip, reduce or cancel easily
missing_sip_controls.definition: The investor wants to pause, skip, change the amount or date, or cancel, but the option is missing, broken or deliberately hard, so they cancel outright or feel trapped.
missing_sip_controls.question: stop

app_reliability_errors.name: App bugs, slow processing and confusing status
app_reliability_errors.definition: SIP orders stay in processing, units are allotted late, the app crashes or an update breaks flows, or the investor cannot tell whether a SIP is active or where money went after cancelling.
app_reliability_errors.question: stop

fees_paywall.name: New fees, paywalls and upselling
fees_paywall.definition: The platform starts charging for basics, locks features behind subscriptions or pushes paid plans, and the investor stops or moves SIPs.
fees_paywall.question: stop

support_trust_breakdown.name: Unresponsive support and loss of trust
support_trust_breakdown.definition: Problems go unresolved because support or the agent does not respond, and the investor loses trust in the platform.
support_trust_breakdown.question: stop

returns_disappointment.name: Disappointing returns or market fear
returns_disappointment.definition: Flat, negative or below-expectation returns over months or years, or fear during market falls, lead the investor to stop or consider stopping.
returns_disappointment.question: stop

cash_need_affordability.name: Cash need or amount too high
cash_need_affordability.definition: The investor needs the money elsewhere, or the SIP amount (or step-up) becomes hard to sustain.
cash_need_affordability.question: stop

platform_or_fund_initiated.name: Stopped or changed by the platform or fund
platform_or_fund_initiated.definition: The SIP was paused, deleted or cancelled by the fund house or platform rather than by the investor.
platform_or_fund_initiated.question: stop

switching_plan_or_platform.name: Switching plan, fund or platform (not a real drop)
switching_plan_or_platform.definition: The investor stops a SIP only to restart it elsewhere, e.g. regular to direct, a different fund or another app.
switching_plan_or_platform.question: stop

early_confusion_first_months.name: Early confusion after the first instalment
early_confusion_first_months.definition: In the first weeks or months after starting, the investor misunderstands how the SIP works (when instalments are taken, where the money is, what cancelling or redeeming does) and stops or cancels as a result.
early_confusion_first_months.question: behaviour

return_expectations.name: Specific return expectations at the start
return_expectations.definition: Starts with a concrete expectation of returns or a corpus (e.g. 12% a year, 1 crore in 10 years), often set by ads or creators.
return_expectations.question: start

missed_reminders_forgetting.name: No reminders, so instalments are forgotten
missed_reminders_forgetting.definition: Instalments are missed because the app sends no reminder or due-date notification, and the investor forgets to pay or place the order.
missed_reminders_forgetting.question: stop

disruptive_app_updates.name: App updates that break or hide SIP flows
disruptive_app_updates.definition: A redesign or update removes or hides SIP features (pay button, SIP list, modify, tracking), so the investor misses payments, cannot manage SIPs or decides to leave.
disruptive_app_updates.question: stop

charges_lockin_surprise.name: Surprise charges, lock-ins or tax at exit
charges_lockin_surprise.definition: The investor is surprised by exit loads, lock-in periods, tax or other charges when stopping or redeeming, and feels misled.
charges_lockin_surprise.question: stop

conflicting_advice.name: Conflicting or misleading advice
conflicting_advice.definition: The investor is confused or loses confidence because creators, agents or ads give conflicting or misleading messages about SIPs, or they were mis-sold (e.g. a regular plan without understanding it).
conflicting_advice.question: behaviour

long_term_discipline.name: Long-term discipline (protective)
long_term_discipline.definition: Investor keeps going because of a long horizon, a family goal, discipline or experience of holding through falls.
long_term_discipline.question: behaviour

corrections: Example quote for `missing_sip_controls` was "no option to stop a sip without redeeming"
Replaced with "Cannot pause the sip in the App" (FundsIndia, Play Store)

The original quote was cut out of context. Without explaining that 'stopping' means ending future instalments while 'redeeming' means selling units, it read as nonsensical. An example has to be clear without the full review.

Theme `setup_onboarding_friction` mixed barriers to starting (initial investment, KYC, minimum amounts) with early confusion after starting; example was "Concept of initial investment is totally unacceptable"
Renamed to `early_confusion_first_months`; pre-start barriers moved out of scope; example replaced with a first-time investor confused about the next instalment who then cancelled (TradingQ&A)
The study is about first-time investors who have already started and then stop within ~12 months. An initial-investment complaint is about starting, not stopping.
`long_term_discipline` was proposed as a theme to be scored and ranked with the drop-off themes
Kept only as a contrast (protective) theme: shown in the dropper-vs-continuer table, excluded from the ranked opportunity list
The goal is to find what causes drop-off; a protective factor ranked as a "priority" would be misleading.
limitations: Reddit was not used: its API needs approval and scraping is barred by its terms. X, Instagram and Quora were also not used (no permitted access).

Reviews and forum posts are not a random sample of investors. App-store reviews skew towards complaints, so product friction is over-represented relative to behavioural reasons such as returns or cash needs.

Droppers come mostly from app-store reviews and continuers mostly from YouTube, so stop-lift partly reflects which source a theme appears in, not only stopping behaviour. Read stop-lift as directional.

SIP status, first-time status and time since starting are self-reported. Only 7 records say the writer is a first-time investor and 84 state how long they have invested, so the 12-month view is descriptive only.
'Stopped' includes stopping SIPs on a platform; people who only moved to another app are excluded from the dropper group where switching was their only stop reason.

Coding was done by Claude (Opus) inside a Claude Code session, not via an API, because the Gemini key had no credits. The same model designed the prompts and did the coding; the golden set is the independent check.
Evidence-span checks were run by the coder before submitting answers, so the 100% span pass rate reflects that self-check; the pipeline still verifies every span in code.
The golden set is small (20 records), so per-field agreement has wide uncertainty.
Most store reviews come from apps other than Groww (Coin, ET Money, FundsIndia, Paytm Money and others). Findings describe first-time SIP investing in India generally, not Groww specifically.
